newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-GERMAN TRIO MAKE BIG WIMBLEDON RAID.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GERMAN TRIO MAKE BIG WIMBLEDON RAID.

text.p: Boris Becker, Michael Stich and teenager Nicolas Kiefer led a spectacular German advance into the Wimbledon quarter-finals on a showery afternoon on Tuesday.

Becker's straight sets victory over Chile's Marcelo Rios and Stich's earlier four-set win over Mark Woodforde once again demonstrated that the former champions have not lost their touch on the All England Club grass.

But it was the 19-year-old Kiefer's stunning 6-2 7-5 2-6 6-1 win over world number three Yevgeny Kafelnikov which grabbed most attention prior to the Centre Court 'match of the day' between defending champion Richard Krajicek and local hero Tim Henman.

Kiefer, a former junior finalist at Wimbledon, had already beaten Alexander Volkov and Andrei Medvedev on his way to the fourth round, but his latest performance was easily the best result of his senior career and also ensured the most Germans in the last eight at a grand slam in the Open era.
Only on-court treatment for a lower back problem and a rain delay at 3-1 in the final set threatened to delay his march into the last eight, where he will meet Australian Todd Woodbridge.

"To be in the quarter-finals of Wimbledon is great," said Kiefer, one of the first two players to be accepted into the recently-formed Becker junior team in Germany. "Woodbridge is a good player but I have a chance."

Becker, who still believes he has a chance to add to his three Wimbledon singles titles, waltzed through the first two sets against Rios, and despite trailing 3-0 in the third, came through unscathed 7-5 in a tiebreak.
"I guess I had a bit too much power for him," he said. "I kept him under constant pressure, but with a bit more practice on grass he has a chance to win here."
He now plays either Pete Sampras or Petr Korda, while his compatriot Stich was waiting to meet the winner of the Krajicek-Henman encounter.

Doubles specialist Woodbridge, meanwhile, earned his first appearance in a grand slam singles quarter-final by defeating compatriot Pat Rafter 6-7 6-4 7-6 6-3 to guarantee at least two unseeded semifinalists.
Either Britain's Greg Rusedski or France's Cedric Pioline will appear in the last four, with Rusedski the clear favourite after his straight sets win over American Richey Reneberg.
The Canadian-reared Rusedski is serving well enough to worry anyone and his 7-6 6-4 7-6 victory was his third straight sets success in four matches.
But Pioline has now reached the last eight for the third time in five years, courtesy of his 3-6 6-3 6-4 7-5 win over New Zealander Brett Steven.

Before Henman's appearance, though, the biggest cheer was reserved for Stefan Edberg who was given a minute-long standing ovation on Centre Court in recognition of his contribution to Wimbledon over the years.
